title: Best Corn-Based Side Dishes for a Texas-Style BBQ
meta_description: Elevate your cookout with the best Texas style BBQ corn sides. From creamy elotes to smoky grilled cobs, discover recipes and tips for the perfect spread.
html:
When you’re firing up the smoker for a Texas-style feast, the meat usually takes center stage. Whether it's a 12-hour brisket or some peppery pork ribs, those rich, smoky flavors need a side dish that can hold its own. Corn is the gold standard here. It provides a natural sweetness and a satisfying crunch that cuts through the heavy fats of the meat.

Finding the right Texas style BBQ corn sides means balancing traditional Southern comfort with a bit of bold, Southwestern flair. Whether you prefer your corn off the cob in a creamy skillet or charred directly over the coals, the goal is to enhance the sweetness of the grain while adding a layer of savory depth.

The Ultimate Grilled Corn on the Cob

You can't have a BBQ without traditional grilled corn. For a true Texas feel, skip the boiling water and go straight to the grill. High heat creates caramelization (the Maillard reaction), which brings out a nutty sweetness that steamed corn just can't match.

For the best results, peel back the husks but leave them attached to the base to act as a natural handle. Soak them in water for 10 minutes to prevent burning, then grill until the kernels are charred in spots. Once removed from the heat, slather them in salted butter and a sprinkle of smoked paprika.

Since grilled corn is notoriously messy, this is where the right tools matter. I always reach for the Interlocking Corn on the Cob Holders (5 Pairs). These Girla holders have bright silicone handles that make them easy to spot on a crowded picnic table, and because they interlock, they don't end up scattered across my kitchen drawers.

Tex-Mex Style Elotes (Street Corn)

While traditional BBQ is essential, no modern Texas spread is complete without Elotes. This Mexican street corn hybrid is a crowd favorite because it hits every taste bud: salty, tangy, creamy, and spicy.

To make these, grill your corn until charred, then coat each cob in a mixture of mayonnaise, sour cream, and lime juice. Roll the cob in crumbled Cotija cheese and finish it off with a dusting of chili powder or Tajín. The creaminess of the sauce pairs perfectly with a sliced brisket sandwich.

Because Elotes are coated in a thick, sticky sauce, using the Interlocking Corn on the Cob Holders (5 Pairs) is a lifesaver. It keeps your hands clean while you enjoy the messiness of the toppings, and when the party is over, you can just toss the holders in the dishwasher.

Creamy Texas-Style Corn Pudding

If you prefer a side that feels more like a comfort food casserole, corn pudding is the way to go. This is a staple at family gatherings across the Lone Star State. It’s essentially a cross between a corn souffle and a savory bread pudding.

The secret to a great corn pudding is using a mix of canned cream-style corn and fresh kernels. This ensures you get a smooth, custardy texture with pops of whole corn for contrast. Bake it in a cast-iron skillet to get those crispy, browned edges that complement the smokiness of the BBQ.

The Best Corn-Based Accompaniments for Texas Style BBQ Corn Sides

Depending on what meat you're serving, you might want to vary your corn preparation. Here are a few quick ideas to round out your menu:

  • Honey-Butter Corn Ribs: Slice corn cobs vertically into quarters to create "ribs" that curl when grilled. Brush with honey butter and sea salt.
  • Corn and Jalapeño Maque Choux: A sauté of corn, bell peppers, onions, and jalapeños for a spicy, chunky side.
  • Grilled Corn Salad: Cut the charred kernels off the cob and toss with feta, cherry tomatoes, and a lime vinaigrette.

Tips for Prepping Corn for a Crowd

Feeding a dozen people can be chaotic. To keep your BBQ stress-free, prep your corn in advance. If you're making a corn salad, grill the cobs the night before and store the kernels in the fridge. For whole cobs, have your butter and seasoning mixtures ready in squeeze bottles or bowls.

Organization is key. Using the Interlocking Corn on the Cob Holders (5 Pairs) allows you to set out a tidy station where guests can grab their own skewers without fumbling through a pile of loose plastic or metal picks. It keeps the presentation polished and the cleanup fast.

FAQ

Should I peel the corn before grilling?

It depends on the result you want. Grilling in the husk steams the corn, keeping it juicy and tender. Peeling the husk allows the kernels to char and caramelize, which provides a deeper, smokier flavor preferred in Texas BBQ.

How do I prevent corn from sticking to the grill?

lightly brush the kernels with oil or melted butter before placing them on the grates. Ensure your grill is preheated to a medium-high temperature so the corn sears quickly rather than sticking.

Can I make corn pudding in advance?

Yes, you can prep the mixture and keep it in the fridge overnight. However, for the best texture and those signature golden edges, bake it shortly before serving so it stays fluffy and warm.
